Print the project's dependencies as a tree.

brickkit.yaml only locks versions; what depends on what is each component's own business, written in its
component.yaml. This command reads it from there — the same resolved graph brickkit graph draws
(uncached manifests are fetched from their install source).

  brickkit deps               one tree per top-level component (nothing in the project depends on it)
  brickkit deps <id>          that component's tree — every version of it in the project — and what requires it
  brickkit deps <id>@<ver>    one version only

A component version is expanded once per output; later occurrences say (shown above).
Weak dependencies say (optional); one that is not in the project says (optional, not installed).

Usage:
  brickkit deps [<id>[@<version>]] [flags]

Examples:
  brickkit deps
  brickkit deps erp/backend
  brickkit deps erp/backend@2.0.0

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for deps

Global Flags:
      --log-level string   Level of the JSON logs on stderr (debug | info | warn | error | off) (default "off")
